messages:
maria (Support): FYI escalation from ACME — streaming SSE session drops mid-request when the client's token rotates. Python SDK iterator never yields the final chunk, customer sees truncated output and reports duplicate billing for retried chunks. Repro attached, session id 8f7c9a2.

li (Eng-Runtime): Can you paste the short timeline + sample server logs and which model/region? Is this hosted or dedicated?

maria (Support): Hosted us-east1, model: gpt-redwood-3b, session 8f7c9a2. Timeline: token refresh triggered at +46s, server responded 401 at +47s, client reconnected immediately and resumed but final "done" event never observed. Logs (redacted):
```
2025-10-02T15:12:46Z stream[8f7c9a2] token refresh requested
2025-10-02T15:12:47Z stream[8f7c9a2] upstream 401 auth_failed
2025-10-02T15:12:48Z stream[8f7c9a2] client reconnect attempt=1
2025-10-02T15:12:48Z stream[8f7c9a2] event seq=42 partial chunk
```

tia (Eng-ML): Which Python SDK version? We shipped a change to iterator close behavior in 1.4.2 that might be related. Also: any client-side evidence of duplicate sequence numbers?

maria (Support): ACME running python SDK 1.4.2. They captured the SSE stream lines; saw seq=42 repeated after reconnect: `seq=42 -> seq=42 -> seq=43`. They think server might be re-sending a partial chunk.

jonathan (DevEx): Poking at the iterator code now. Recent abort/refill change added a path where we drop the final partial frame when a 4xx occurs midstream. Minimal repro I ran locally:
```
# pseudo
for chunk in client.stream("/v1/streams", token=short_lived):
    print(chunk)
# when token rotates mid-emit, iterator stops without emitting final "done" marker
```

deploy-bot: deploy finished: infra/runtime-hotfix-2025-10-02-07 ✔️

li (Eng-Runtime): Sounds like two issues: 1) reconnect + resume ordering can cause the client to see a repeated seq and drop the later "done" because it thinks it's a duplicate; 2) billing double-count if server replays same token'ed chunks. Need logs with event IDs or raw SSE lines to confirm. Can QA attach tcpdump or raw SSE transcript?

maria (Support): Attached raw SSE transcript (snippet):
```
event: chunk
data: {"seq":42,"text":"...partial"}

event: info
data: {"status":401}

(reconnect)

event: chunk
data: {"seq":42,"text":"...continuation"}
event: chunk
data: {"seq":43,"text":"..."}
event: done
data: {}
```

jonathan (DevEx): That transcript explains it — the client dedupe logic treats seq=42 as already consumed (it saw the partial) and throws away the continuation. The iterator close path also suppresses emitting the final `done` on 4xx. Two causes stack. I'll prototype a fix to merge partial frames and ensure `done` is emitted on reconnect when a resumed stream completes.

lia (sic?) (typo)

tia (Eng-ML): Workaround for CS to give customer: increase auth refresh window or use longer-lived token to avoid rotation during the request. Also set client option `allow_resume_dedupe=false` if available (we can add flag). This is short-term only.

sarah (Customer Success): Customer is asking about billing — they saw token-triggered replays counted twice. Can we pause billing for session 8f7c9a2 until we confirm dedupe and replay behavior? They want an ETA before we escalate to finance.

li (Eng-Runtime): I don't have billing write perms, but I can open a hotfix and a billing investigation ticket. Hotfix ticket created: INFR-1429, assigning to eng-runtime, will target a patch that: 1) merge partial seq frames on resume, 2) ensure `done` is propagated even if a 4xx occurred during the handshake.

jonathan (DevEx): I'll prepare a PR for the Python SDK iterator to land the merge and add tests for midstream 401 and seq dupes. ETA for review: ~4 hours, QA tomorrow morning. I'll also add a runtime flag to opt into stricter dedupe handling.

maria (Support): Thanks — Sarah, I told ACME we have a hotfix ticket and a patch is being prepared. For immediate mitigation I recommended: pin token to longer TTL and add client-side buffer to accept duplicate seqs until final `done`. They accepted temporary workaround.

li (Eng-Runtime): Billing inquiry opened: BILL-8813 linking INFR-1429. Suggest we set a one-time credits hold for ACME while we confirm replay charges — @sarah can you request credits hold with finance and reference BILL-8813?

sarah (Customer Success): On it, pinged finance with the session id and tickets. I'll update the customer once finance confirms.

maria (Support): Marking thread for follow-up. Thanks all, will paste PR/patch links when available. :pray:
